target.name: Electric Sheep
target.founder: Gunjit Singh, Jarrett Herold, Naganand Murty

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $26M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Electric Sheep, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Gunjit Singh, Jarrett Herold, and Naganand Murty, has raised $25.5M to date. Valuation analysis relies on a peer set of 9 comparable companies across robotics and manufacturing—1 public and 8 private—including Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics at valuations ranging from $1.1B to $2.0B, primarily at Series B stage.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression modeling applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, using the $25.5M raised as a value proxy, yielding $51M. Peer-median analysis across the 4-company comparable set (Generalist AI at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B, Walden Robotics at $1.1B) produces a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range of $1.1B–$2.0B. The substantial divergence between methods reflects stage and maturity differences; peer companies skew toward Series B, where valuations have compressed materially relative to earlier frontier-tech peaks.

The analysis supports a range of $43M to $2.0B, with a triangulated median of $876M. Key uncertainties include capital intensity and path-to-profitability in hardware robotics, the relevance of Series B comparables to an early-stage Series A position, and whether peers' recent financings reflect market repricing or selection bias.
